subproblem.title: Mass of a difference is at most the sum of the masses (fact (F1); Simon Ch. 6, 2.5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Then M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) in [0, ∞]. Conventions: 𝒟_n(U) is the space of n-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) and 𝒟ⁿ(U) the test n-forms in U (TestFormOn U n: smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U, a submodule of the space of forms); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G; massAdmissibleOn U n G); A − B is the contract instance Sub, whose underlying linear functional is ω ↦ A(ω) − B(ω).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (A - B).massOn G ≤ A.massOn G + B.massOn G
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F1) of the parent proof, i.e. the triangle inequality for Simon's mass 6.2.5 (M_G is a supremum over admissible forms), as used in Simon's proof of Theorem 6.7.2.
1. By definition M_G(A − B) = sup{ofReal((A − B)(ω)) : ω admissible for M_G}. By the least-upper-bound property (sSup_le) it suffices to fix an admissible ω and prove ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B).
2. −ω is admissible for M_G. Indeed 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a submodule, so −ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and its underlying form is the pointwise negative of the underlying form of ω. Hence tsupport(−ω) = tsupport(ω) ⊆ G (tsupport_neg), and for every x, |(−ω)(x)| = |−(ω(x))| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1, because the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under negation (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
3. (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) by the definition of the contract instance Sub, and B(−ω) = −B(ω) because the underlying functional of B is linear. Hence (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω).
4. For real s, t one has ofReal(s + t) ≤ ofReal(s) + ofReal(t) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). With step 3, ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A(ω)) + ofReal(B(−ω)).
5. Every admissible value is bounded by the corresponding mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn): ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) because ω is admissible, and ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_G(B) because −ω is admissible by step 2. Adding these two bounds to step 4 gives ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B); by step 1, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible ω, since M_G(A − B) is a supremum over admissible forms.
−ω is admissible: the same topological support and a negation-invariant Euclidean coefficient norm.
(A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ofReal is subadditive.
Bound ofReal(A(ω)) by M_G(A) and ofReal(B(−ω)) by M_G(B).

audit.reason: The one-line type exactly matches the statement for arbitrary U and G, without additional openness or finiteness assumptions. Negating an admissible form preserves its support and coefficient-norm bound; linearity, ofReal subadditivity and the supremum bound prove the conclusion. The proof is complete and non-circular. Its two applications establish finite boundary mass before the parent's use of BR.
